name: Digital Credentials API (mDL and wallet IDs)
plain: Lets a site ask for a government ID or other credential from a digital wallet.
meaning: Requests only fields the person approves (age over 21, name, address) from a wallet such as Google Wallet or Apple Wallet, with a browser prompt.

access.prompt_ui: Browser wallet picker plus per field consent in the wallet
access.iframe: Same as top level; cross-origin iframes need a permissions policy where listed

data.metric: Lets a site ask for a government ID or other credential from a digital wallet.

limits.headline: Can ask for facts from your digital ID, only the ones you approve
limits.user_action: You tap Verify with ID and approve each item in your wallet
can: Ask your wallet for one fact such as age over 21, name or address
Receive only the fields you approve in the wallet
Prove you are an adult or a resident without handing over the whole ID
cannot: See your full ID card or photo when you approve only one field
Get anything without your approval in the wallet
Work in Firefox or Safari on most devices today
Keep the ID facts after the check unless the site chooses to store them
limits.reach_label: Only the ID fields you approve
limits.differs: Chrome and Edge support it. Safari support is partial. Firefox does not.

story.what_it_is: A site can ask your phone wallet for a government ID, with you approving what is shared.

marketing.name: Digital Credentials API
marketing.pitch: Chrome describes it as a way for sites to request verified documents like a driver's license from a wallet, with the person in control.

marketing.name: Verify with Wallet
marketing.pitch: Apple pitches showing ID in Wallet to apps and sites, sharing only the details a person approves.

story.for_you: A prompt appears on your computer or phone asking if you agree to share things like 'over 21' from your wallet ID. You scan a code or tap and approve with Face ID. Nothing is shared until you agree.
story.for_makers: Makers use it for age checks, account opening and fraud checks without collecting photos of ID. It lowers risk and cost, and they store less data about the person.

use_cases.example: An online liquor or vape shop asks wallet ID to prove 'over 21' without storing a driver's license photo.
A bank opens an account online by asking the wallet for a verified name and address instead of an upload.
A game or betting site proves a player is an adult with a single wallet approval, with no ID scan.
A car rental site verifies a driver's license from the wallet before it releases the booking.
A social or dating site uses a wallet age check to keep kids out, sharing only the yes or no.
A site checks that the ID is signed by a real government issuer, which stops forged scans.

risks: Oversharing if you approve too much

technical_bounds: Android needs Play services 24.0 or newer; desktop uses QR plus BLE proximity
Spec still a W3C Working Draft

abuse: Over collection of personal data by relying parties

history.change: Digital Credentials ships (OpenID4VP and ISO 18013-7 Annex C)
